name: SEO Content Refresh
description: A reviewed page-edit plan, verified changes when authorized, or a later performance check. Each change keeps its source, review and verification record.
audience: SEO and content teams improving existing pages
problem: Content refreshes turn into broad rewrites when search intent, current performance, technical issues, and conversion purpose are not diagnosed first.
outcome: A reviewed page-edit plan, verified changes when authorized, or a later performance check. Each change keeps its source, review and verification record.
whyAi: AI can compare search evidence, page structure, project context, and editorial constraints while keeping the final judgment and publication boundary explicit.
operatorPath: Example request: “Use SEO Content Refresh on [page URLs]. Readers should be able to try each method. Keep the URLs and useful links. Show the proposed edits and checks before changing the site.”
Choose the job: prepare a plan, apply reviewed edits, or assess an earlier refresh. Preparation is the default; applying changes needs permission and a usable editing route.
Provide current page content, the reader or business goal, and available search or analytics evidence. For an assessment, include the earlier change record and baseline.
Check the actual edits and the later performance result separately. A page can be successfully updated while its search impact is still unknown.
agentPath: Confirm the pages, business goal and whether the job is to prepare edits, apply them or assess an earlier refresh. Review existing content and comparable search data.
Find the reader or technical problem before proposing exact page and link edits. Have the proposal independently reviewed and resolve the findings before applying it.
Apply only authorized changes, check each result, and keep records of completed, failed or uncertain edits. Inspect an uncertain result before retrying. Preparation stops with the reviewed plan.

When assessing an earlier refresh, compare later data with the saved baseline and explain the measurement limits. Record inconclusive results when the data cannot support a conclusion, and leave the content unchanged.
recovery: Preserve applied and unknown change receipts; inspect actual current state before retrying an uncertain action.
If inputs, authorization or destination checks are missing, retain a prepared/blocked packet and exact repair steps.
Resume delayed measurement from the prior refresh ref in assess mode, preserving original implementation evidence.
If no changes are confirmed applied, route follow-up to apply or a blocked implementation handoff; schedule assess only after actual implementation exists.
safeStoppingPoints: Prepare closes with the reviewed exact proposal and explicit next_mode apply implementation prerequisite; no implementation means no scheduled outcome assessment.
Apply closes with verified or explicit partial implementation and outcome pending when no valid later window exists.
Assess closes with observed or inconclusive outcome and never reapplies changes.

handoffs.when: Repository changes need engineering delivery or a shared-template/technical change exceeds the bounded refresh.

prerequisites: Existing page URLs and the reader or business problem to solve
Current page content and available search or analytics evidence, from connected tools or approved exports
To apply changes: an accepted edit plan, permission and a supported editing route. To assess changes: the earlier record, baseline and a comparable later data window.
proof: A reviewed proposal with the exact old and new wording, the reason for each edit, useful links to preserve and the checks to run.
Illustrative edit: a workflow guide says “write clear requirements” but gives no usable brief. Add the task, inputs, acceptance checks and a saved handoff while preserving the page's purpose and URL.
For applied work, a record of each completed, failed or uncertain edit and a check of the actual page. A successful build alone does not establish what readers can see.
A separate performance assessment using the saved baseline and a comparable later window. If the sample is too small or the data incomplete, the result stays pending or inconclusive.
One saved refresh record that connects the proposal, review, actual changes, verification and next measurement step.
whenToUse: Existing pages or their internal connections need bounded evidence-led improvement.
A prior refresh needs outcome assessment without reapplying changes.

stages.title: Recover Scope And Mode
stages.summary: Normalize one bounded page set and recover prior proposals/receipts before new work.

stages.title: Collect Baseline Or Follow-Up Evidence
stages.summary: Capture the smallest useful native/source-export evidence set with comparable metadata.

stages.title: Diagnose Before Editing
stages.summary: Separate intent, technical, content, internal-link and measurement issues.

stages.title: Prepare Exact Multi-Page Changes
stages.summary: Make each edit reviewable against current source content and destination evidence.

stages.title: Review And Adjudicate The Proposal
stages.summary: Independently review before applying and preserve one canonical reviewed version.

stages.title: Apply Authorized Changes Or Preserve Preparation
stages.summary: Perform only current accepted edits inside the explicitly authorized boundary.

stages.title: Verify Each Changed Page
stages.summary: Prove implementation independently of delayed performance effects.

stages.title: Assess Outcomes Or Schedule Follow-Up
stages.summary: Compare only sufficiently observed, comparable windows and state uncertainty honestly.

stages.title: Store The Canonical Refresh And Follow-Up
stages.summary: Make future recovery and delayed measurement possible without replaying edits.
